task_instruction: Rewrite each direct yes/no question as a reported question.
paragraphs: At an observatory, Dr. Ruiz interviews astronomer Maya Chen about a new research project. The next morning, Maya writes a summary of their conversation. Dr. Ruiz asked Maya, {{red:Have you identified a possible exoplanet?}} {{mask_1}} Maya had found a promising signal in the data. Dr. Ruiz asked, {{red:Does the signal repeat at regular intervals?}} {{mask_2}} She explained that repeated dips in a star's brightness could suggest a planet passing in front of it.

Dr. Ruiz asked Maya, {{red:Did you compare the observations from both telescopes?}} {{mask_3}} She had compared them the previous night. Dr. Ruiz then asked, {{red:Are you checking the measurements for instrument errors?}} {{mask_4}} Maya was reviewing the calibration records. He asked, {{red:Have you ruled out changes in the star itself?}} {{mask_5}} Maya said that the team was still investigating that possibility.

The interview moved to the team's methods. Dr. Ruiz asked Maya, {{red:Will the observatory collect more data next month?}} {{mask_6}} The team had booked additional observation time. He asked, {{red:Can your team use spectroscopy to study the planet's atmosphere?}} {{mask_7}} Maya said that the equipment could analyze light from the distant system. Dr. Ruiz asked, {{red:Have you estimated the planet's orbital period?}} {{mask_8}} Maya had calculated an early estimate but wanted more observations.

Dr. Ruiz asked Maya, {{red:Would you describe the current result as preliminary?}} {{mask_9}} Maya said that more evidence was needed. He asked, {{red:Could the telescope observe the target star again tonight?}} {{mask_10}} The forecast suggested that clouds might arrive. Dr. Ruiz asked, {{red:Did the team include the uncertainty range in its report?}} {{mask_11}} Maya confirmed that the report included it. He also asked, {{red:Are the raw observations available to other researchers?}} {{mask_12}} Maya explained that the data would be shared after review.

Their discussion turned to how astronomers check an unusual result. Dr. Ruiz asked Maya, {{red:Has another observatory confirmed the signal?}} {{mask_13}} No independent team had confirmed it yet. He asked, {{red:Do you think the signal could come from a binary star?}} {{mask_14}} Maya said that the team had tested that explanation. Dr. Ruiz asked, {{red:Will you publish the analysis if the evidence remains strong?}} {{mask_15}} Maya said that the team planned to submit its work for peer review.

At the end of the interview, Dr. Ruiz asked Maya, {{red:Have you prepared a diagram of the star's light curve?}} {{mask_16}} She had made a clear graph for the presentation. He asked, {{red:Can you explain why the star becomes slightly dimmer during a transit?}} {{mask_17}} Maya said she could explain the observation with a simple model. Dr. Ruiz asked, {{red:Are you presenting the results at the astronomy meeting next week?}} {{mask_18}} Maya said that she was preparing a presentation. Before they left, he asked, {{red:Would you like us to include your team's data in the public archive?}} {{mask_19}} Maya agreed, provided the final paper cited the team. Dr. Ruiz asked one last question, {{red:Do you expect the next observation to clarify the signal?}} {{mask_20}} Maya said that it might provide useful evidence.
